title: Prohibition on avoiding a reporting requirement
definition: The prohibition on breaking up or structuring a transaction, or a series of transactions, so as to avoid a reporting or recordkeeping requirement that would have applied to the transaction as a whole. The prohibition applies to the purpose, so the pattern of conduct and the surrounding facts matter, and not only the amounts. Conduct by a person associated with a financial institution, but not by the institution itself, is covered by a separate provision. This record summarises the prohibition.
evidence_to_cite: the individual transactions, each cited by its own source id
the reportable transaction they would have formed, if it had been made in one
the facts relied on to establish purpose, and their source

sources.citation: Definitions governing the avoidance of reporting requirements (31 CFR 1010.100), summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: The prohibition is about purpose, which is why a pattern of small transactions is not by itself a violation, and why the surrounding facts have to be evidenced.
